The 331/334/358/640-pixel checks are from current hash-bound render metadata and independently checked SVG font scaling. No additional mobile, product or theme screenshot was opened or claimed.
method.routing: All four figures are deterministic instructional apparatus diagrams. Source objects are manufactured geometric structures; no natural-artwork generation or hybrid layer is needed.
method.sourceConsumption: The previously consumed six pages and eleven raw PNGs remain carried forward. The four original figure opens are the specifically authorized comparisons for new figures, not another page/crop approval round.

method.machineEvidence: Read-only verify.mjs checks current hashes, inventory resolution, all 702 current geometric assertions, all directed arrow mappings, world-space projection equations and source-critical apparatus junctions. verify-svg.py parses actual SVG XML to distinguish hidden construction colors from visible semantic colors. Neither script opens an image into context, renders a new candidate, writes evidence, or substitutes for the eight visual inspections.

fig243And244.coordinateConvention: World axes are right-handed. Canvas user y increases upward; bitmap y is the negative of user y.
fig243And244.cameraCheck: Both camera rows have norm one and dot product zero, so this is a valid orthographic projection.
fig243And244.loop: r(t)=(0,R cos(t),R sin(t)). The basis cross product e_y cross e_z is +e_x; r cross dr/dt=(R^2,0,0). Increasing t therefore selects +e_x as the conventional-current normal.
fig243And244.projection: The projected circle is (0.6 R cos(t), R sin(t)), with the figure's translation added. All two Fig243 and three Fig244 contour radii satisfy this construction in the actual current coordinates. This is a disclosed consistent reconstruction, not a uniquely recovered camera or measured source aspect ratio.
fig243And244.currentSigns: At the left rim, t near pi gives downward motion; at the right rim, t near zero gives upward motion. All six displayed rim arrows have positive signed area in the normalized world y-z plane: approximately 0.4168708, 0.4168708, 0.47942554 in each figure. This confirms their sense independently of the renderer's endpoint equality checks.
fig243And244.normalSign: P(+e_x)=(0.8,0), so the selected normals point right. The current normal arrow displacements are positive-x in both actual specs. No claim of perpendicularity between an ellipse and a horizontal arrow on the page is used.
fig243And244.screwSign: The Fig243 lower-right turning head advances upward around the shaft with the same positive y-z circulation. A right-handed screw then advances along +e_x, the shaft and pointed right tip. The turning indicator is a schematic gesture, not a measured circular cross section or thread pitch.
fig243And244.needleSign: Fig244's explicit S-left and N-right pole labels fix the S-to-N direction. The needle arrow and loop normal both have positive horizontal displacement. The spec's parallel assertion alone would also accept opposite signs; the independent signed check and actual pole/arrow inspection remove that ambiguity.

stableExternalField.derivation: For a small planar current loop in an approximately uniform external field, m=I A n and U=-m B cos(theta). The stable energy minimum is theta=0, so the current-selected normal aligns with external B; anti-alignment is an unstable extremum. The same stable S-to-N orientation applies to a magnetic needle.
stableExternalField.limits: A rotating loop's instantaneous normal is not automatically external B. Neither a source-free field arrow nor a polarity is inferred in Fig242. Fig243 explains current selection, not a specific external field. Fig244 is interpreted with the already-PASS stable-settling text, not as an arbitrary transient.
stableExternalField.currentConvention: Conventional current is used; electron-motion direction is not substituted.

fig245.cameraCheck: Rows are orthonormal: 0.8*(-0.24)+0.6*0.32=0 and each squared norm is 1.
fig245.axesDerivation: World e_y dot e_z=0. Their screen-up projections are (0.6,0.32) and (0,sqrt(0.84)), which are not perpendicular on the page. Obliqueness of the bearing guide is compatible with a physically horizontal axis and does not turn it into another tilted or vertical physical axis.
fig245.coilBasis: The coil plane is spanned by e_y and w=(-sin(beta),0,cos(beta)). These unit vectors are perpendicular, so the authored contours are projected circles, not distorted arbitrary ellipses. All 216 contour segments match this equation.
fig245.dipAndSign: One of the two admissible plane normals has negative world z, compatible with the regional downward inclination discussed in the text. The source gives no current or pole sign to select one normal, and the current figure correctly adds no n, B, current or numerical dip. No unique field direction or universal terrestrial dip is claimed from these pixels.
fig245.largerCoilCondition: The comparatively large Earth-field demonstration coil remains subject to the already-PASS requirement that the external field be approximately uniform over it.

displayAndColor.fig242NullReason: There are no visible text labels to shrink or read in Fig242; null is not a zero-size text measurement.
displayAndColor.visualCollisionAssessment: The actual final bitmaps are nonblank and unclipped. Current heads and normal/needle arrows are distinct, the screw remains recognizable, pole/vector labels do not cover apparatus, and the two added axis labels fit inside Fig245 without overlapping its coil or lead. Intended wire/support/axis intersections are not treated as label collisions.
displayAndColor.svgLiteralColorAssessment: The XML contains default #D55E00 construction elements, but every such element is display:none or visibility:hidden. Visible literal-color elements are zero in every current SVG. Visible geometry uses semantic CSS variables; arrow markers inherit context-stroke. No source polarity is inferred from color alone.
displayAndColor.themeAndPrintScope: Semantic-role and inherited-marker structure is verified; source distinctions remain readable from outline, letters and arrow direction rather than hue. No separate alternate-theme or print raster inspection is claimed.
displayAndColor.culturalLeakage: None observed. No Cyrillic, Chinese, Soviet symbols, handwriting, source texture, flags, uniforms or fictional cultural elements were copied into the outputs.
displayAndColor.sourceGridOrTickRequirements: None in these four originals. The Fig245 axis guides are modern additions, not an omitted or invented source scale.

figures.independentSourceInventory: One horseshoe magnet opening left, with two long parallel arms, a curved common joining body at the right, thickness and both free-end faces; one small rectangular loop hangs between the open ends from a vertical textured strand. The near arm is dark and rear arm light. No pole letters, current heads, normal, B, dimensions, numbers, axes, battery or hand are visible.
figures.sourceRolesAndPositions: Both arms are one body, not separate magnets. The loop is within the physical open gap near the left ends; its side edges and the strand are vertical in projection, and the strand meets its top edge. The original strand's electrical-versus-mechanical role is not resolved by pixels and is not relabeled with an invented terminal or current.

inventoryMapping.assessment: Parallel arms, complete four-edge loop closure and strand/top-edge incidence are checked, not replaced with objectCount. The single joined U body and loop-in-gap placement are independently confirmed from source pixels, current polygon geometry and the final bitmap.

findings.observation: The actual repaired bitmap shows a clear open separation between the suspended loop and near free-end face. No loop corner suggests mechanical contact. Independently computed minimum loop-to-magnet boundary centerline clearance is 39.36 px; allowing the two stroke radii leaves 35.36 px of ink gap, or 18.28775 px at the narrowest declared 331-pixel display.

The repaired figure preserves the source's unlabeled apparatus. It adds no made-up N/S pole, current, B or selected normal; no polarity is guessed from the arm shading. Projection and smoothing are disclosed modern layout choices, not source measurements.

figures.independentSourceInventory: Left: projected loop with winding contours, two upper leads, downward left and upward right current indications, I by the upper lead, left-side downward rim heads and an opposed right-side upward head; a rightward normal with vector-n label. Right: shaped thick vertical screw handle, horizontal shaft ending in a rightward point, shaft texture/thread indication, and a curved turning indicator with its visible lower-right head directed upward. No hand, measured angle or external-field label is present.
figures.sourceRolesAndPositions: Both upper lead feet meet the loop's top region; the left lead supplies downward conventional-current indication and the right upward indication. The rightward normal starts inside the loop, and the screw shaft/point share its projected direction. The curved screw-turn head is not substituted for the real handle and shaft. Fine unreadable source texture is not decoded as exact thread pitch or turn count.

inventoryMapping.assessment: All visible objects and directed arrows resolve to inventory mappings. Actual contour equations, positive world y-z current signs and real screw geometry are independently checked; the collinear and endpoint assertions are not mistaken for an RHR proof.

findings.observation: Actual left-down/right-up rim heads, upper-lead current indications, rightward n, screw shaft and upward lower-right turning head agree with the independently derived +world-x normal. The n label is below-right of the loop edge without collision; both I and the vector arrow over n are visible.

The current bitmap retains both upper leads and the physical handle, threaded/marked shaft and pointed tip. Lead-foot-to-outer-coil centerline distances are about 1.8968 and 1.1768 px, below the combined 3.5-pixel stroke radii, confirming the visually continuous joins. Smooth contours and schematic thread/turning marks are disclosed regularization, not measured source dimensions.

figures.independentSourceInventory: Two side-by-side objects in a comparative frame: a double-ended horizontal magnetic needle with S on the light left half, N on the dark right half, concentric central pivot and a small rightward centerline arrow; a tall multi-contour loop to the right with downward left current indications, opposed circulation on the right, a filled center dot and thick rightward vector-n arrow. No separate field label, apparatus support, axis scale or dimension is present.
figures.sourceRolesAndPositions: S and N are source poles, unlike unlabeled Fig242. Their S-to-N direction agrees with the stable loop's current-selected normal. The pivot, coil center and two orientation arrows remain visible. Clear source left-side current heads establish the sense; coarse or damaged fine arrow texture is not assigned an invented contrary direction.

inventoryMapping.assessment: All objects are mapped, and pole/arrow direction is independently assessed rather than inferred from color or a sign-blind parallel assertion. Source-required pivot, filled coil center, both needle halves and complete winding contours are retained.

findings.observation: In the actual current bitmap, S is left, N is right, the needle centerline arrow points right, and the loop has left-down/right-up circulation and rightward selected n. These signs agree with the world-space derivation and stable-equilibrium text. Pole letters, pivot and vector n are separated and legible.

Three regularized winding contours preserve the source's multi-contour structure without claiming an exact source turn count. Moving pole letters above the needle is disclosed readable layout, not a changed pole or physical axis. No B label, universal field, numerical angle or support was invented.

figures.independentSourceInventory: One inclined multi-contour circular coil leaning upper-left to lower-right; a supporting inverted-U yoke around its upper region; a vertical shaft from the arch to a short thick horizontal top bar; opposed left-lower and right-upper coil attachments, the left with an angular bracket; a wavy lead from the right attachment rising to a thick free end at upper-right. There are no readable current, pole, n, B, rotation, axis labels, turn count or numerical dip in the source.
figures.sourceRolesAndPositions: The shaft provides the vertical turning axis. The opposed coil bearings provide one physically horizontal axis, although oblique in the projection. Both bearings, the left bracket, yoke, shaft, bar and full visible right lead are retained. The electrical return circuit or a hidden second lead cannot be recovered from these pixels and is not invented.

inventoryMapping.assessment: Mapped endpoint and axis assertions have actual apparatus meaning. Independent checks additionally verify both yoke-to-bearing joins, both outer-coil-to-bearing joins, the world-top yoke-to-shaft join, every wavy-lead segment join, and lead-to-right-bearing/free-end incidence. Counts alone do not establish fidelity.

findings.observation: The actual final bitmap retains the complete inclined coil, surrounding yoke, top support bar, connected shaft, both bearings, projecting left bracket, continuous wavy right lead and thick free end. No connection required by the visible source has been dropped. Apparent wire/yoke crossings are intentional projected apparatus intersections, not missing leads or label collisions.

The dashed vertical guide follows the shaft and the diagonal guide follows both bearings. Independent 3D evaluation confirms perpendicular physical vertical/horizontal axes and a coil plane able to tilt about the bearing axis. No screenshot-perpendicular illusion, invented measured dip, selected-current sign or pole is used.

Vertical axis and Horizontal axis are English modern labels paired with the two added dashed guides; neither is claimed to be a source inscription. Both labels are complete, readable and outside the coil/lead footprints. The cleaned camera, illustrative tilt and normalized contour radii are layout data, not source-given dimensions or Earth-field measurements.
